models.name: Qwen2.5-Coder 1.5B Instruct (Q4_K_M)
models.summary: Starter: small and fast; good for small code bases, shallower explanations.

models.name: Qwen2.5-Coder 3B Instruct (Q4_K_M)
models.summary: Between the 1.5B and the 7B: noticeably better than the 1.5B and still fast on 8 GB PCs. Its licence does not allow commercial use.

models.name: Phi-4-mini 3.8B Instruct (Q4_K_M)
models.summary: Microsoft's small general model. Not offered for log diagnosis: in testing it ignored the report format and cited evidence that does not exist.

models.name: Gemma 3 4B Instruct (Q4_K_M)
models.summary: Google's small general model: clear, readable explanations of what went wrong.

models.name: Qwen2.5-Coder 7B Instruct (Q4_K_M)
models.summary: Standard: clearly better reasoning about code; a good default for medium code bases.

models.name: Llama 3.1 8B Instruct (Q4_K_M)
models.summary: Meta's widely used general model; a different view from the Qwen coders at the same size.

models.name: Gemma 3 12B Instruct (Q4_K_M)
models.summary: Strong general reasoning for explaining failures; dense, so slower than the 7B and 8B models.

models.name: DeepSeek-Coder-V2-Lite 16B Instruct (Q4_K_M)
models.summary: Mixture-of-experts coder: about 2.4B parameters work per word, so it is fast on a CPU, with 7B-class code skills.

models.name: Qwen2.5-Coder 14B Instruct (Q4_K_M)
models.summary: Large, dense: strong reasoning but every answer uses all 14B parameters, so it is slow on a CPU.

models.name: Phi-4 14B (Q4_K_M)
models.summary: Microsoft's 14B reasoning model; strong at working out causes, but slow on a CPU like other dense 14B models.

models.name: Qwen3-Coder 30B-A3B Instruct (Q4_K_M)
models.summary: Large, mixture-of-experts: the strongest here, yet only ~3B parameters work per word, so it answers about as fast as a small model. Needs plenty of RAM.

models.name: Qwen2.5-Coder 32B Instruct (Q4_K_M)
models.summary: The strongest dense coder here, best for careful conversions; every word uses all 32B parameters, so it is very slow on a CPU. Needs 32 GB+.

tasks.name: Log root-cause diagnosis
tasks.no_workload_hint: Build or open a knowledge base and the advisor will tell you whether your code base is large enough for a bigger model to be worth downloading.

tiers.label: small
tiers.explain: A small model can follow a code base of this size.

tiers.label: medium
tiers.explain: At this size a 7B model reasons noticeably better about how the parts fit together.

tiers.label: large
tiers.explain: A large code base benefits from the strongest model this PC can run.

tasks.name: Code conversion (e.g. C++ to C#, Python 2 to 3)
tasks.no_workload_hint: Point the advisor at the source to convert and it will size the model to the largest file, which has to fit in the model's context together with its translation.

tiers.label: small
tiers.explain: Short files convert well with a 7B model; a 1.5B model tends to drop details when rewriting code.

tiers.label: medium
tiers.explain: Files of this length need a model that keeps the whole file consistent while rewriting it.

tiers.label: large
tiers.explain: Some files are longer than the context window: they are converted in pieces, so the strongest model helps keep the pieces consistent.
